### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** N/A (a code map): the driver chooses the time step, executes every stage, checks for rejection and writes accepted states; there is no main time loop inside a block.
**Data.** In: a block or mesh, the integration limits and the output schedule. Out: accepted states written by `make_outputs`, the final write and the exit reason.
**Placement.** The outermost loop of a run: `max_time_step`, the stages, `check_redo`, `make_outputs`, `finalize`.
**Activation.** Caller supplied; the integration defaults belong to pyharp.
**Guarantee / limits.** A map; no convergence order. The example applies kinetics after all dynamics stages and before the rejection decision.
**Evidence.** `test_restart_cycle_limit` (resume cycle and logged values, absolute $10^{-12}$, time $10^{-9}$); `test_check_redo_parallel.release` (collective redo and rollback, exact); `driver_check.py` `[C1]`-`[C3]` (clock, step halving and stop, on a port of the loop).
:::

The driver chooses the time step, executes every stage, checks rejection, and writes accepted states. There is no main
time loop inside a MeshBlock. The C++ example applies kinetics after all dynamics stages and before the rejection
decision.

### Derivation

No separate derivation: this section describes an interface or control-flow path. Numerical operators are derived in
their owning chapters.

The loop's bookkeeping is checked on a port of the driver loop. A rejected step leaves the clock and the cycle
count where they were, and outputs follow only accepted steps [check `src/snapy_report/ch01/driver_check.py`,
output `driver_check.out`, `[C1]`]. Each redo halves the step of the retry (`[C2]`). A negative `check_redo` ends
the loop at the time of the last accepted step (`[C3]`).

### Numerical method

The driver keeps the clock unchanged when a step is rejected. A positive return from `check_redo` repeats the cycle; a
negative return ends it. `max_time_step` first reduces the local hydro limit with MIN, then applies the Courant factor
and the redo halving. Outputs are scheduled after the accepted clock increment. The `straka` driver also writes
immediately after initialization, including restart. No independent spatial or temporal order belongs to this control
flow; it inherits the selected operators.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The restart writer saves output counters before `make_outputs` increments them. Together with the unconditional
initial output in `straka`, this is a code-level reason to investigate repeated restart outputs; no overwrite
experiment is reported here. Driver-split kinetics is outside the MeshBlock stage.
:::
